In [[abstract algebra|algebra]], an '''SBI ring''' is a type of [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' (with identity) such that every [[idempotent (ring theory)|idempotent]] of ''R'' [[modulo (jargon)|modulo]] the [[Jacobson radical]] can be [[lift (mathematics)|lifted]] to ''R''. The abbreviation SBI was introduced by [[Irving Kaplansky]] and stands for "suitable for building idempotent elements".{{sfnp|Jacobson|1956|p=53|ps=}}

== Definition ==
{{needs expansion|date=March 2026}}

== Examples ==
* Any ring with [[Nil ideal|nil]] radical is SBI.
* Any [[Banach algebra]] is SBI: more generally, so is any [[Compact space|compact]] [[topological ring]].
* The ring of [[rational number]]s with [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] denominator is not SBI.
